questions.q: According to this lesson's decision framework, what should you check first before reaching for Python?
options: Whether Power Query (runs once, shapes data before load) or DAX (recalculates live, per filter/click) already covers the need
Always start with Python regardless of the task
Check DAX only — Power Query is never relevant to this decision
The framework recommends picking randomly among the three
questions.explain: The framework explicitly checks Power Query and DAX first — Python is the answer only when the task genuinely needs something neither built-in tool can do.

questions.q: Why might using a Python script to rename a column be the wrong choice, even though it works?
options: If Power Query's UI already does it in a few clicks, a Python script adds a dependency (a working Python install on every refreshing machine) for zero real benefit
Python cannot actually rename columns at all
Power Query is technically incapable of renaming columns
There is no reason to prefer Power Query in this case
questions.explain: Technical capability isn't the only consideration — reaching for Python when a simpler built-in tool already solves the problem adds unnecessary complexity and a maintenance dependency.

questions.q: Why is DAX still non-negotiable for certain calculations, even after learning Python?
options: DAX recalculates live, per filter context, as a user interacts with a report; Python runs once and produces only a static result
DAX and Python are functionally interchangeable for every use case
Python is actually faster than DAX for all live calculations
DAX has been fully replaced by Python as of this course
questions.explain: This is the same distinction Lesson 1 introduced — nothing about learning Pandas changes DAX's unique ability to respond live to user interaction.

questions.q: What is a genuine example from this course of Python filling a real gap, not just a preference?
options: Lesson 18's fillna(method='backfill') predictive fill — a data-cleaning technique with no simple Power Query equivalent
Renaming a single column
Filtering rows where a value is greater than 100
Sorting a table alphabetically
questions.explain: A predictive fill technique like backfill is a genuine capability gap — the kind of task that's a few lines of Pandas versus a dozen awkward Power Query steps, not something equally easy either way.

questions.q: What is the overall point of this final lesson?
options: To provide a framework for correctly choosing between Power Query, DAX, and Python based on what a task actually needs — not defaulting to whichever tool was learned most recently
To argue that Python should replace Power Query and DAX entirely
To argue that Python has no legitimate use in Power BI at all
To recommend using all three tools simultaneously on every task
questions.explain: The lesson's core message is deliberate tool selection based on what the task genuinely requires — using Python where it earns its place, not out of habit or recency.
